methods.name: Stage-Progression

data.narrative:
Walden Robotics, a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Russ Tedrake (MIT professor and ex-SVP Large Behavior Models at Toyota Research Institute), is valued at $1.1B post-money on $300M total raised. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of nine same-sector peers spanning Seed through Series F stages, including eight private companies (Divergent at $2.3B, Exotec and Locus Robotics at $2.0B each, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B) and one public comparable.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, implies $2.8B. Peer-median analysis across nine robotics companies with similar valuation tiers yielded $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. The peer set reflects meaningful heterogeneity in development stage, suggesting some comparability discount is warranted.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $1.5B (low) to $3.2B (high), with a median of $2.2B. The current $1.1B valuation sits materially below the triangulated range, implying either that the last round undervalued the company relative to peer progression, or that the peer set overstates expected value. Key uncertainties include differentiation relative to later-stage competitors and capital efficiency through commercialization.
